statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail remains well below the block threshold while overnight price discovery stays contained and retracements remain available.
recommendation: Overnight NQ futures hold a contained ~0.45% range and have already retraced about 64 points from the overnight high, so no persistent one-way path is observed. Conditional trend-up risk concentrates in the Tuesday US afternoon and is expressed as a narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC danger window rather than a session-wide restriction.
headline: Contained, thin-liquidity overnight range after Monday's record chip-led close; Tail low with a narrow Tuesday afternoon protective band
body:
Monday closed the Nasdaq-100 at a record 30,482.35 (+2.83%, +838 points), with the Nasdaq Composite also at a record and the S&P 500 up about 1.5%, driven by a repricing of CPU and AI demand that lifted Intel about 12%, AMD about 10% and Meta about 11%, with the semiconductor index up over 3%. NDX still sits roughly 1% below its 30,762.20 52-week high. Overnight, NQ futures trade near 30,853 (+0.22%) inside a contained range of about 138 points (~0.45%), and price has already retraced about 64 points from the 30,916.50 overnight high after printing near 30,898 an hour earlier. That is two-way discovery in which retracement is available, not the shallow-pullback, failed-retracement structure that denies mean reversion. An important qualifier is liquidity: Tokyo cash equities are closed for three consecutive sessions (Respect for the Aged Day, a Citizens' bridge holiday and the Autumnal Equinox), with only Osaka derivatives trading, so the contained overnight range is less informative about conviction than a normal Asian session would be.

Cross-asset confirmation is only partial, which argues for Stress over Tail. VIX is near 14.87, close to the lower end of its recent range. Treasury yields are high but eased on Monday, with the 10-year near 4.96% against a 5.01% H.15 reading for September 18 and the 2-year near 4.76%, so rates are not aligned behind an equity squeeze. The policy backdrop is genuinely hawkish: the FOMC raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.0% on September 16, its first increase since 2023, on a unanimous 12-0 vote, and the Summary of Economic Projections points to one further hike in 2026. Energy is the live two-sided channel. WTI is near $93 (+0.9%) and Brent near $101.50 (+1.2%), rebounding modestly after four consecutive declining sessions driven by hopes that diplomacy around the UN General Assembly, whose general debate opens today, can de-escalate the US-Iran conflict. Tehran has not confirmed reciprocal interest, so the risk premium that has been coming out of crude could return abruptly.

The dominant forward catalyst is the Trump-Xi summit in Washington, with the arrival ceremony reported for Wednesday, the main bilateral meeting Thursday and a state dinner attended by AI and chip executives. The agenda spans trade, Taiwan, AI and rare-earth export controls, and reporting notes that no major breakthrough is expected. Because its exact timing is not firmly established, it is described here as a checkpoint rather than entered in the verified calendar. Tuesday's own calendar is light: the Richmond Fed survey at 14:00 UTC, Fed speakers Williams, Jefferson and Barkin, and a 2-year note auction at 17:00 UTC. None of these is a Tail block on its own.

The shared Finviz cross-asset context was unusable for this run: the file is about four hours old, its collection status is partial, and its futures and calendar sections are explicitly marked unavailable. This assessment therefore rests entirely on independent primary-source research, which is current and broad enough to support high Confidence. Tail is held at 12 because nothing in the observed price path shows persistent one-way structure, while Stress at 34 reflects a stretched index, a hawkish rate path near 5% on the long end, and unresolved energy geopolitics. Conditional trend-up risk is concentrated in the Tuesday US afternoon and expressed as a narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC band.

lookbackSummary: Past 24h: Monday's US session ran a chip-led trend-up regime that lifted Tail from single digits in the Asian hours to an intraday peak of 33 around 19:00 UTC, with Stress reaching 57 and the mapped policy state passing through yellow into orange between 14:00 and 19:00 UTC. That regime then decayed in an orderly way into the close, Tail falling to 23 by 20:00 UTC and 14 by 21:00 UTC, which is the signature of a trend day that still permitted retracement rather than a no-retracement path. The last seven hours have been a stable green overnight base, Tail oscillating between 11 and 13 and Stress between 32 and 35, with dominant mode normal throughout.
outlookSummary: Base case is a calm, thin overnight continuation with Tail in the low band and mode normal while Tokyo cash stays shut. The forecast tilts conditionally higher through the European session and into the Tuesday US cash open at 13:30 UTC, entering the watch band from 14:00 UTC and peaking in a narrow protective band between 15:00 and 17:00 UTC, which defines the danger window. That band assumes an opening-continuation scenario with shallow pullbacks toward the 30,762.20 cash 52-week high; it is protective rather than observed and decays quickly if orderly retracement appears. Checkpoints inside the window are the Richmond Fed survey, Fed speakers Williams, Jefferson and Barkin, and the 17:00 UTC 2-year auction. Risk then decays through the power hour into the 20:00 UTC close and returns to the base level overnight, with the Wednesday flash PMI and the Trump-Xi summit falling outside this 24-hour window.
